Average seconds between queued and completed per exporter in the past 14 days?
SELECT
  "exporter",
  AVG(("completed" - "queued") / 1000.0) AS "avg_seconds"
FROM "network_flows_daily"
WHERE "__time" >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '14' DAY
  AND "queued" IS NOT NULL
  AND "completed" IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1

v2_train_05155 - For last month, list the repository_name, commit_hash, and artifact_size_mb for the top 2 builds with the larg
exact_column pipe_table last_period moderate 7265 tok 3 tables calendar_window
For last month, list the repository_name, commit_hash, and artifact_size_mb for the top 2 builds with the largest artifact_size_mb per repository_name.
WITH "ranked_builds" AS (
  SELECT
    repository_name AS "repository_name",
    commit_hash AS "commit_hash",
    artifact_size_mb AS "artifact_size_mb",
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY repository_name ORDER BY artifact_size_mb DESC) AS "rn"
  FROM ci_pipeline_daily
  WHERE __time >= TIME_SHIFT(TIME_FLOOR(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'P1M'), 'P1M', -1)
    AND __time < TIME_FLOOR(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'P1M')
)
SELECT
  "repository_name",
  "commit_hash",
  "artifact_size_mb"
FROM "ranked_builds"
WHERE "rn" <= 2
ORDER BY 1, 3 DESC

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Clickstream events from a consumer web app, enriched with device and experiment data. Each row is one event. Prefer this table whenever the question is about web / product analytics activity rather than a pre-aggregated summary. Don't wrap `user_id` in COUNT(DISTINCT ...). It is already unique, so a simple row count gives the number of events. The exact number of distinct session ids is required, so write COUNT(DISTINCT `session_id`). **Glossary** - **UK-or-Japan event**: records where `country_code` is `GB` or `JP` - **referrer-host-series event**: any row in which `referrer_host` matches the prefix pattern 'face%' ### Columns: `__time` (TIMESTAMP, NOT NULL): Ingested event time. Becomes `__time`, the only TIMESTAMP column. `session_id` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): Opaque session identifier. `user_id` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): Hashed user identifier. High cardinality. `event_type` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): One of: page_view, add_to_cart, checkout, purchase, search. `page_path` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): URL path of the page the event fired on. `country_code` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code. `device_type` (VARCHAR, NOT NULL): One of: desktop, mobile, tablet. `browser` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): Browser family. `os_name` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): Operating system family. `referrer_host` (VARCHAR, NOT NULL): Hostname of the HTTP referrer. `ab_bucket` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): A/B assignment bucket: control, variant_a, variant_b. `latency_ms` (BIGINT, NOT NULL): Server-side request latency in millis

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Tracking ticket purchases for live events. Each row is one ticket sale. Prefer this table whenever the question is about live-event ticket sales activity rather than a pre-aggregated summary. 1. `created_by_id` is unique per row in this table. Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Records of physical and digital items borrowed by library patrons. This is the event-level table for public library lending: high volume, one row per loan. A question asking for a running total or a current snapshot may be better served by a dimension table instead. ### Instructions * Reports quote unique item barcodes to the exact number. Avoid APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT on `itemBarcode`. We treat a row as a Panel-L loan when `branchLocation` is `south_hills`, `west_valley` or `digital_portal`. We treat a row as a high-fee-accrued loan when `lateFeeAccrued` > 4. We treat a row as a genre-classification-series loan when `genreClassification` begins with 'sci_'. - __time :: TIMESTAMP - Time the item was borrowed by the patron. Becomes `__time`, the only TIMESTAMP column. - materialFormat :: VARCHAR - Physical or digital format of the borrowed item. - audienceCategory :: VARCHAR - Target age group for the material (possible values: children, young_adult, adult, senior). - branchLocation :: VARCHAR - Library branch where the checkout occurred. - genreClassification :: VARCHAR - Primary literary genre or category. - itemBarcode :: VARCHAR - Unique identifier affixed to the physical or digital copy. - loanDurationDays :: BIGINT - Allowed checkout period in days. - lateFeeAccrued :: DOUBLE - Monetary penalty accumulated for overdue return. - itemWeightGrams :: BIGINT - Physical weight of the item in grams. - answerTime :: BIGINT - When the request was answered, stored as epoch seconds ( ASSIGNED TERM (like_prefix): genre-classification-series loan -- the SQL must apply exactly this definition

How many unique machines had Set-J turbine readings in the past 7 days?
WITH "filtered_data" AS (
  SELECT "turbineId"
  FROM "windTurbinesRaw"
  WHERE "__time" >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '7' DAY
    AND "farmLocation" = 'baltic_coast'
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT "turbineId") AS "unique_machines"
FROM "filtered_data"

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Periodic sensor readings from wind turbines across various wind farms. Use this table for questions scoped to wind-farm turbine telemetry; it is the system of record for individual turbine readings, not a daily rollup. Unique turbine ids = exact COUNT(DISTINCT `turbineId`). Sketch-based approximations are not acceptable. -- Set-J turbine reading means records where `farmLocation` equals `baltic_coast`. -- Engaged turbine means a distinct `turbineId` seen at least once during the past 90 days. __time TIMESTAMP The exact time the telemetry snapshot was captured farmLocation VARCHAR The geographic site of the wind farm (one of: north_sea_offshore, texas_plains, scottish_highlands, mojave_desert, baltic_coast) turbineState VARCHAR windDirection VARCHAR Cardinal direction the wind is blowing from bladePitchMode VARCHAR The current aerodynamic control mode turbineId VARCHAR Unique identifier for the physical turbine powerOutputKw DOUBLE Instantaneous active power generated in kilowatts windSpeedMps DOUBLE Measured wind speed in meters per second rotorRpm DOUBLE Rotational speed of the main rotor weatherConditionsJson VARCHAR Local atmospheric conditions queued VARCHAR When the item was queued

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Edge cache access records from a content delivery network. Each row is one edge request. Prefer this table whenever the question is about CDN edge delivery activity rather than a pre-aggregated summary. -- 1. Reports quote unique updated by ids to the exact number. Avoid APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT on `updated_by_id`. -- 2. v2_train_04138 - For backup-power tower samples this year, rank departments by highest estimated unique baseband IP addresses,
business yaml this_period simple 24385 tok 6 tables approx calendar_window
For backup-power tower samples this year, rank departments by highest estimated unique baseband IP addresses, having over 2.
SELECT
  department_code AS "department",
  APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(baseband_ip) AS "unique_ips",
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(baseband_ip) DESC) AS "rank"
FROM ds_cell_tower_kpis
WHERE __time >= TIME_FLOOR(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'P1Y')
  AND power_status = 'generator'

This is the event-level table for mobile network cell-tower KPIs: high volume, one row per tower sample. A question asking for a running total or a current snapshot may be better served by a dimension table instead. **Rules** - Precision matters for updated by ids: use exact distinct counting on `updated_by_id`. - When you compute anything from `uplink_bytes`, include the condition uplink_bytes IS NOT NULL so blanks don't dilute the result. ### Glossary * backup-power tower sample = rows where `power_status` is `generator` * uplink-to-downlink ratio = total `uplink_bytes` divided by total `downlink_bytes` * high-call-rate tower sample = records where `dropped_call_rate` > 4 columns: - name: __time type: TIMESTAMP description: "Time the performance metrics were aggregated. Becomes `__time`, the only TIMESTAMP column." - name: band_class type: VARCHAR description: "Frequency band classification (values: low_band, mid_band, high_band, mmwave)." - name: connection_tech type: VARCHAR description: "Generational technology standard (values: 3g, 4g_lte, 5g_nsa, 5g_sa)." - name: power_status type: VARCHAR description: "Power supply source for the site (possible values: mains, battery, generator, solar)." - name: antenna_vendor type: VARCHAR description:

Prefer this table whenever the question is about live-event ticket sales activity rather than a pre-aggregated summary. ### Instructions * Since every record carries its own created_by_id, distinct counting on created_by_id is unnecessary and should be avoided. * Reports quote unique owner ids to the exact number. Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Telemetry and meter reads from municipal water network endpoints. This is the event-level table for water utility network metering: high volume, one row per meter read. A question asking for a running total or a current snapshot may be better served by a dimension table instead. ### INSTRUCTIONS * No DISTINCT needed (or wanted) when counting meter reads via `endpointMac`: the values are one-per-record. * Numeric rollups of `linePressurePsi` (sum, average, min, max) exclude rows where `linePressurePsi` is NULL. A Set-Q meter read is any record where `pressureZone` is in ('high_elev_1', 'high_elev_2'). A Pod-K meter read is any record where `customerClass` is `agricultural` and either `linePressurePsi` is greater than 90 or `meterModel` is `ultrasonic_plus`. | Column | Type | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | __time | TIMESTAMP | Time the telemetry packet was recorded by the meter. Becomes `__time`, the only TIMESTAMP column. | | customerClass | VARCHAR | Billing classification of the metered endpoint. | | meterModel | VARCHAR | Hardware model of the smart water meter (one of: aqua_smart_x1, flow_pro_200, hydro_sense_v3, legacy_mech_4, ultrasonic_plus). | | pressureZone | VARCHAR | Hydraulic zone within the distribution network. | | batteryStatus | VARCHAR | Health indicator for the meter power source. | | endpointMac | VARCHAR | Network identifier of the smart meter radio module. | | gallonsConsumed | BIGINT | | | flowRateGpm | DOUBLE | Instantaneous flow rate in gallons per min ASSIGNED TERM (mixed): Pod-K meter read -- the SQL must apply exactly this definition

Guard duration math with an `endedAt` IS NOT NULL predicate: a missing end time means not finished. **Glossary** - **Segment-7 playback heartbeat**: records where `cdnProvider` is `akamai` or `inhouse` - **active profile**: a distinct `profileId` seen at least once during the past 30 days - **high-rebuffer playback heartbeat**: any row in which `rebufferMs` is no less than 5400 - __time (TIMESTAMP) - Time the playback heartbeat was recorded - titleId (VARCHAR) - Catalogue title being watched (possible values: t-100, t-101, t-102, t-103, t-104, t-105, t-106, t-107) - deviceClass (VARCHAR) - Playback device family - cdnProvider (VARCHAR) - CDN serving the segments (one of: akamai, fastly, cloudfront, inhouse) - streamQuality (VARCHAR) - Ladder rung in use - profileId (VARCHAR) - Viewer profile identifier - watchSeconds (BIGINT) - Seconds watched in this heartbeat window - rebufferMs (BIGINT) - Milliseconds spent rebuffering - bitrateKbps (BIGINT) - Delivered bitrate - playerJson (VARCHAR) - JSON payload held as text - received (VARCHAR) - Upstream receive time, held as day-first t

  SELECT
    TIME_SHIFT(TIME_FLOOR(MILLIS_TO_TIMESTAMP("finish_ts"), 'P1M'), 'P1M', 1) AS "next_month",
    "vibration_amplitude"
  FROM "wind_turbines_daily"
  WHERE "blade_pitch_mode" = 'feathered'
)
SELECT

  AVG("vibration_amplitude") AS "avg_vibration"
FROM "shifted_telemetry"

v2_train_05586 - What was the daily total data volume and average flow latency for 'ingress' traffic last month?
vocab_gap druid_native last_period moderate 6847 tok 8 tables calendar_window time_bucket
What was the daily total data volume and average flow latency for 'ingress' traffic last month?
WITH "daily_metrics" AS (
  SELECT
    TIME_FLOOR(__time, 'P1D') AS "flow_day",
    SUM("bytes") AS "total_volume",
    AVG("duration_ms") AS "avg_latency"
  FROM "network_flows_daily"
  WHERE "direction" = 'ingress'
    AND __time >= TIME_SHIFT(TIME_FLOOR(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'P1M'), 'P1M', -1)
    AND __time < TIME_FLOOR(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'P1M')
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  "flow_day",
  "total_volume",
  "avg_latency"
FROM "daily_metrics"
ORDER BY 1

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Edge cache access records from a content delivery network. Each row is one edge request. Prefer this table whenever the question is about CDN edge delivery activity rather than a pre-aggregated summary. Approximations are banned on updated_by_id. Count its distinct values exactly. Guard duration math with a `completed` IS NOT NULL predicate: a missing end time means not finished. Definitions: spotlight edge request is any row in which `client_country` is in ('IN', 'SG', 'US'); other-client-country edge request is rows where `client_country` is not `BR`; Tier-C edge request is rows where `protocol` is one of `h2`, `h3`, `http1.1`. columns: - name: __time type: TIMESTAMP description: "Time the edge node served the object. Becomes `__time`, the only TIMESTAMP column." - name: pop_code type: VARCHAR description: "Point-of-presence that served the request." - name: content_type type: VARCHAR description: "MIME family of the object (one of: image, video, script, html, font, json)." - name: protocol type: VARCHAR description: "" - name: client_country type: VARCHAR description: "" - name: object_key type: VARCHAR description: "Cache key of the requested object. High cardinality." - name: origin_host type: VARCHAR description: "Origin the edge would fall back to." - name: ttfb_ms type: BIGINT descript

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Per-request records from a public API gateway. Use this table for questions scoped to API gateway traffic; it is the system of record for individual API requests, not a daily rollup. 1. Approximations are banned on external_ref_id. Count its distinct values exactly. 2. Never use COUNT(DISTINCT `request_trace_id`) here: values of `request_trace_id` never repeat. | Term | Definition | | --- | --- | | Group-R API request | Records where `route_template` is `/v1/inventory/{sku}` or `/v1/accounts/{id}` | | retry-count-to-gateway-latency ratio | Total `retry_count` divided by total `gateway_latency_ms` | | high-response API request | Records where `response_bytes` > 270150 | | api-name-family API request | Rows where `api_name` starts with `ship` | - __time :: TIMESTAMP - Time the gateway accepted the request. Becomes `__time`, the only TIMESTAMP column. - api_name :: VARCHAR - Logical API the route belongs to. - route_template :: VARCHAR - Matched route pattern. - auth_mode :: VARCHAR - How the caller authenticated. - client_tier :: VARCHAR - Rate-limit tier of the calling client. - client_id :: VARCHAR - Calling client identifier. High cardinality. - upstream_host :: VARCHAR - Backend instance that served the call. - gateway_latency_ms :: BIGINT - Time spent inside the gateway. - upstream_latency_ms :: BIGINT - Time spent waiting on the backend. - response_bytes :: BIGINT - Response body size in bytes. - rate_limit_remaining :: BIGINT - Quota left in the caller's window. - policy DECOY (real_column): the word 'premium' defines nothing; the SQL must not add a glossary filter

For travel purchases on Visa over the past 90 days, what is the estimated number of unique merchants and the most recent fraud score?
WITH "filtered_txns" AS (
  SELECT
    "__time",
    "merchantId",
    "riskScore"
  FROM "ds_fin_txn"
  WHERE "merchantCategory" = 'travel'
    AND "cardNetwork" = 'visa'
    AND __time >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '90' DAY
)
SELECT
  APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT("merchantId") AS "estimated_merchants",
  LATEST("riskScore") AS "latest_fraud_score"
FROM "filtered_txns"

Use this table for questions scoped to API gateway traffic; it is the system of record for individual API requests, not a daily rollup. **Rules** - How many unique external ref ids? Answer with COUNT(DISTINCT `external_ref_id`); estimates are not acceptable. - `request_trace_id` identifies a single record. Counting by it must not use DISTINCT. If someone says "Group-R API request", they mean records where `route_template` is `/v1/inventory/{sku}` or `/v1/accounts/{id}`. If someone says "high-response API request", they mean any row in which `response_bytes` is above 270150. Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Interval readings from residential and commercial smart meters. Each row is one meter reading. Prefer this table whenever the question is about smart metering activity rather than a pre-aggregated summary. # **Rules** # - To count meter readings, use COUNT(*) or COUNT(accountRef); the column is unique, so DISTINCT would only add cost. # - Don't let missing kwhConsumed values leak into averages; filter on kwhConsumed IS NOT NULL before aggregating it. # Count something as a Basket-M meter reading when `tariff` is one of `flat`, `dynamic`. # Count something as a meter-id-family meter reading when `meterId` matches the prefix pattern 'm-001%'. __time TIMESTAMP meterId STRING tariff STRING premiseType STRING gridZone STRING accountRef STRING kwhConsumed DOUBLE kwhExported DOUBLE voltageV DOUBLE queued STRING datasource: ds_logistics # Scan events from a parcel and freight network. This is the event-level table for freight logistics: high volume, one row per parcel scan. A question asking for a running total or a current snapshot may be better served by a dimension table instead. # **Rules** # - Keep only rows where is_test_record = 0, which leaves out test rows. Also, avoid COUNT(DISTINCT `created_by_name`); each value appears once. # If someone says "Italy-or-Ireland parcel scan", they mean records where

v2_train_02082 - For Panel-X predictions, what is the 90th percentile of model response time and estimated unique serving hosts
business no_system none complex 861 tok 1 tables approx
For Panel-X predictions, what is the 90th percentile of model response time and estimated unique serving hosts for each model? Rank these models by their 90th percentile response time from slowest to fastest.
WITH "model_stats" AS (
  SELECT
    model_name AS "model",
    APPROX_QUANTILE_DS(inference_ms, 0.9) AS "p90_inference",
    APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(replica_host) AS "hosts"
  FROM ds_ml_inference
  WHERE model_version IN ('v3', 'canary', 'v2')
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  "model",
  "p90_inference",
  "hosts",
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "p90_inference" DESC) AS "primary"
FROM "model_stats"
ORDER BY 4 ASC

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Per-request telemetry from an online model serving tier. Use this table for questions scoped to ML serving; it is the system of record for individual predictions, not a daily rollup. - There is exactly one row for each created_by_name; a plain COUNT is correct and DISTINCT is unnecessary. - For unique request ids, always use exact `COUNT(DISTINCT request_id)`. Never APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT. Definitions: Panel-X prediction is records where `model_version` is `v3`, `canary` or `v2`; Bucket-D prediction is records where either `outcome` = 'timeout' or `sla_breached_flag` = 0; Group-3 prediction is any row in which both hold: `accelerator` is `l4`, and at least one of (`confidence` is no less than 0.7, `outcome` is `fallback`). - __time (TIMESTAMP) - Time the prediction was served - model_name (VARCHAR) - Model that served the request - model_version (VARCHAR) - Deployed version tag (one of: v1, v2, v3, canary) - accelerator (VARCHAR) - - request_source (VARCHAR) - Caller surface (one of: batch, online, shadow, replay) - outcome (VARCHAR) - How the request finished - request_id (VARCHAR) - Request identifier - replica_host (VARCHAR) - Serving replica - inference_ms (DOUBLE) - - queue_ms (DOUBLE) - - input_tokens (BIGINT) - Tokens in the request payload - confidence (DOUBLE) - Top-class confidence, 0 to 1 - feature_flags (VARCHAR) - Multi-value dimension. Serving flags active on the request - end_time (VARCHAR) - - owner_id (VARCHAR) - Current

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Interval readings from residential and commercial smart meters. This is the event-level table for smart metering: high volume, one row per meter reading. A question asking for a running total or a current snapshot may be better served by a dimension table instead. ### Instructions * Counting distinct legacy_id values? Use COUNT(DISTINCT legacy_id) -- approximate aggregators are not allowed on this column. * Duration metrics only make sense for completed rows: `ended_at` must be NOT NULL. | Term | Definition | | --- | --- | | Cohort-5 meter reading | Records where `grid_zone` is `south_west` or `wales` | | processing-attempts-to-power-factor ratio | Total `processing_attempts` divided by total `power_factor` | | Pod-A meter reading | Rows where `quality_flag` is `estimated` or `is_backfilled` is 1 | | spotlight meter reading | Records where `quality_flag` = 'substituted' AND (`kwh_exported` > 2 OR `premise_type` = 'industrial') | ### Columns: `__time` (TIMESTAMP, NOT NULL): Start of the metering interval. Becomes `__time`, the only TIMESTAMP column. `meter_id` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): Meter that produced the reading. `premise_type` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): Kind of premise (one of: residential, small_business, industrial). `grid_zone` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): Distribution zone. `quality_flag` (VARCHAR, NOT NULL): Reading quality. `account_ref` (VARCHAR, NOT NULL): Billing account reference. `kwh_exported` (DOUBLE, NOT NULL): Energy exported back to the grid. `voltage_v` (DOUBLE, NOT NULL):

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: User workout session telemetry and performance tracking. Each row is one workout. Prefer this table whenever the question is about fitness app workouts activity rather than a pre-aggregated summary. ### Instructions * Exclude soft-deleted records always (keep rows where `is_deleted` = 0). * No DISTINCT needed (or wanted) when counting workouts via `created_by_email`: the values are one-per-record. **Glossary** - **Tier-X workout**: records where `activity_type` is `yoga` or `weightlifting` - **reference-set workout**: records where either `completion_status` = 'aborted' or `is_test_record` = 0 - __time :: TIMESTAMP - When the user initiated the workout session. Becomes `__time`, the only TIMESTAMP column. - activity_type :: VARCHAR - Primary physical activity performed (one of: running, cycling, swimming, yoga, weightlifting, hiit). - workout_environment :: VARCHAR - Where the workout took place. - device_type :: VARCHAR - Wearable or tracker used. - goal_type :: VARCHAR - User objective for the session. - completion_status :: VARCHAR - Whether the user finished the planned workout (possible values: completed, aborted, paused_indefinitely). - user_id :: VARCHAR - Account identifier of the fitness app user. - route_id :: VARCHAR - Identifier for the mapped GPS route. - calories_burned :: BIGINT - Estimated energy expenditure. - average_heart_rate :: BIGINT - Mean beats per minute during the activity. - elevation_gain_meters :: BIGINT - Total climbing altitude in meters. - achi

v2_train_05122 - For Family-N listen events this month so far, what is the total play length in seconds and average completion
vocab_gap sample_rows this_period moderate 13060 tok 5 tables calendar_window
For Family-N listen events this month so far, what is the total play length in seconds and average completion rate by department, ordered highest to lowest by total play length?
WITH notable_events AS (
  SELECT
    department_code,
    duration_listened_seconds,
    completion_rate
  FROM ds_podcast_analytics
  WHERE __time >= TIME_FLOOR(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'P1M')
    AND is_deleted = 0
    AND listening_platform = 'pocket_casts'
)
SELECT
  department_code AS "department",
  SUM(duration_listened_seconds) AS "total_play_length",
  AVG(completion_rate) AS "avg_completion_rate"
FROM notable_events
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC

v2_train_01429 - For yesterday's Group-8 ATM transactions, what are the top 2 hardware models for each card network, ranked by
business verbose_rules day moderate 790 tok 1 tables approx calendar_window
For yesterday's Group-8 ATM transactions, what are the top 2 hardware models for each card network, ranked by the estimated number of unique terminals?
WITH model_stats AS (
  SELECT
    card_network,
    atm_model,
    APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT(terminal_id) AS "unique_terminals"
  FROM atm_network_daily
  WHERE __time >= TIME_FLOOR(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'P1D') - INTERVAL '1' DAY
    AND __time < TIME_FLOOR(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'P1D')
    AND card_network IN ('on_us', 'visa', 'mastercard')
  GROUP BY 1, 2
),
ranked_models AS (
  SELECT
    card_network,
    atm_model,
    "unique_terminals",
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY card_network ORDER BY "unique_terminals" DESC) AS "rn"
  FROM model_stats
)
SELECT
  card_network,
  atm_model,
  "unique_terminals"
FROM ranked_models
WHERE "rn" <= 2
ORDER BY 1, 3 DESC

Becomes `__time`, the only TIMESTAMP column. - atm_model :: VARCHAR - Hardware model of the terminal. - card_network :: VARCHAR - The network processing the card (one of: visa, mastercard, amex, discover, on_us). - auth_result :: VARCHAR - Whether the transaction was approved or declined. - currency_code :: VARCHAR - Local currency of the ATM. - terminal_id :: VARCHAR - Unique identifier for the ATM hardware. - customer_account_id :: VARCHAR - Hashed identifier for the customer account. - amount_dispensed :: DOUBLE - The actual monetary amount dispensed. - surc

v2_train_04556 - What are the top 2 content formats by total user complaints each month for intellectual-property moderation ac
business ddl this_period moderate 395 tok 1 tables calendar_window time_extract_format
What are the top 2 content formats by total user complaints each month for intellectual-property moderation actions this year? Only include formats where average AI certainty exceeds 0.8.
WITH monthly_stats AS (
  SELECT
    TIME_FORMAT(__time, 'yyyy-MM') AS "month",
    contentType AS "format",
    SUM(reportCount) AS "total_reports"
  FROM contentModerationRaw
  WHERE __time >= TIME_FLOOR(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'P1Y') AND reportReason = 'copyright'
  GROUP BY 1, 2
  HAVING AVG(confidenceScore) > 0.8
),
ranked_formats AS (
  SELECT
    "month",
    "format",
    "total_reports",
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "month" ORDER BY "total_reports" DESC) AS "rn"
  FROM monthly_stats
)
SELECT
  "month",
  "format",
  "total_reports"
FROM ranked_formats
WHERE "rn" <= 2
ORDER BY 1, 3 DESC

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Records of warranty service requests filed by consumers. Use this table for questions scoped to consumer-electronics warranty claims; it is the system of record for individual warranty claims, not a daily rollup. **Rules** - Exact cardinality only for `claimId`: COUNT(DISTINCT), no sketches or approximations. **Glossary** - **target-list warranty claim**: records where `warrantyTier` equals `extended` - **claim-status-series warranty claim**: rows where `claimStatus` starts with `under_` - **other-warranty-tier warranty claim**: records where `warrantyTier` is anything other than `standard` - __time :: TIMESTAMP - The date and time the warranty claim was officially submitted. Becomes `__time`, the only TIMESTAMP column. - productCategory :: VARCHAR - The broad category of the consumer device (values: smartphone, laptop, tablet, smartwatch, headphones, television). - claimStatus :: VARCHAR - Current processing phase of the claim. - faultType :: VARCHAR - The reported issue with the device. - warrantyTier :: VARCHAR - The level of coverage the customer purchased. - claimId :: VARCHAR - Unique tracking number for the warranty claim. - repairCost :: DOUBLE - Total cost of parts and labor for the repair. - customerDeductible :: DOUBLE - Out of pocket cost paid by the customer. - turnaroundDays :: BIGINT - Number of days taken to resolve the claim. - loggedAt :: VARCHAR - When the source logged the event, held as date-only text like '2026-03-14'. Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Logs of automated build and deployment pipeline execution. Use this table for questions scoped to CI/CD build pipeline runs; it is the system of record for individual build runs, not a daily rollup. Distinct counts of `previous_owner_id` must be exact: use COUNT(DISTINCT `previous_owner_id`), not an APPROX_ function. Spotlight build run means records where `branch_type` equals `release`. Set-1 build run means rows where `compute_size` is `small` and either `cache_hit_rate` is over 0.4 or `repository_name` is `android_app`. Hit-rate-to-artifact-size ratio means SUM(`cache_hit_rate`) / SUM(`artifact_size_mb`). High-artifact-size build run means records where `artifact_size_mb` >= 130. ### Columns: `__time` (TIMESTAMP, NOT NULL): Time the build job was triggered in the system. Becomes `__time`, the only TIMESTAMP column. `repository_name` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): Target code repository for the build. `build_status` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): Final outcome of the run (one of: success, failed, cancelled, timed_out). `branch_type` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): `compute_size` (VARCHAR, NOT NULL): Resource tier allocated for the build runner. `commit_hash` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): Git commit hash that triggered the build. `runner_node` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): Infrastructure instance that executed the job. `test_coverage_pct` (DOUBLE, NOT NULL): Percentage of codebase covered by unit tests. `artifact_size_mb` (DOUBLE, NOT NULL): Size of the compiled binary or package in megabytes. `cache_hit_rate` (DOUBLE, NO

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Per-request records from a public API gateway. Use this table for questions scoped to API gateway traffic; it is the system of record for individual API requests, not a daily rollup. Include only rows where is_test_record is 0; records created by tests are excluded from every report. Null status_code = unknown, not zero. Exclude NULL rows before you aggregate status_code. A money-movement API request is any record where `api_name` = 'payments'. A Set-K API request is any record where either `auth_mode` = 'mtls' or `sla_breached_flag` = 1. v2_test_heldout_shape_00206 - Which session had the highest-margin line each day in the past 7 days?
business no_system rolling simple 3656 tok 2 tables rolling_window time_bucket time_extract_format
Which session had the highest-margin line each day in the past 7 days?
WITH ranked_sessions AS (
  SELECT
    TIME_FORMAT(TIME_FLOOR(__time, 'P1D'), 'yyyy-MM-dd') AS "day",
    basket_ref AS "session",
    margin_pct AS "margin",
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY TIME_FLOOR(__time, 'P1D') ORDER BY margin_pct DESC) AS "rn"
  FROM ds_retail_pos
  WHERE __time >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '7' DAY
    AND is_deleted = 0
    AND margin_pct IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  "day",
  "session",
  "margin"
FROM ranked_sessions
WHERE "rn" = 1

For Class-E API requests over the past 30 days, what is the daily average proxy delay and count of unique integrators, ordered by day?
SELECT
  TIME_FLOOR("__time", 'P1D') AS "day",
  AVG(gatewayLatencyMs) AS "avg_proxy_delay",
  COUNT(DISTINCT clientId) AS "unique_integrators"
FROM apiGatewayRaw
WHERE "__time" >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '30' DAY
  AND authMode IN ('oauth2', 'mtls', 'anonymous')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Per-request records from a public API gateway. This is the event-level table for API gateway traffic: high volume, one row per API request. A question asking for a running total or a current snapshot may be better served by a dimension table instead. Precision matters for client ids: use exact distinct counting on `clientId`. "Class-E API request" -> records where `authMode` is `oauth2`, `mtls` or `anonymous` "api-name-series API request" -> records where `apiName` begins with 'acco' "Band-K API request" -> rows where `apiName` is one of `webhooks`, `inventory` "gateway-latency-to-upstream-latency ratio" -> SUM(`gatewayLatencyMs`) / SUM(`upstreamLatencyMs`) Columns: __time TIMESTAMP, apiName VARCHAR, httpMethod VARCHAR, routeTemplate VARCHAR, authMode VARCHAR, clientId VARCHAR, statusCode BIGINT, gatewayLatencyMs BIGINT, upstreamLatencyMs BIGINT, created BIGINT Sample rows: 2026-01-10 00:18:13 | accounts | GET | /v1/payments | oauth2 | 0000000167 | 503 | 3 | 521 | 1768004254 2026-05-24 10:14:08 | inventory | POST | /v1/payments | oauth2 | 000000009e | 200 | 4 | 19 | 1779617639 Question: For Class-E API requests over the past 30 days, what is the daily average proxy delay and count of unique integrators, ordered by day? Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Event tracking for property market listings updates and views. Use this table for questions scoped to real-estate listing activity; it is the system of record for individual listing events, not a daily rollup. Finance signs off on the unique mls numbers numbers, so approximations are out; count them with COUNT(DISTINCT `mlsNumber`). Group-V listing event: records where `listingAction` is `price_reduction` or `sold` property-type-series listing event: any row in which `propertyType` matches the prefix pattern 'sing%' high-square-footage listing event: any row in which `squareFootage` is above 6150 | COLUMN_NAME | DATA_TYPE | IS_NULLABLE | DESCRIPTION | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | __time | TIMESTAMP | NO | Moment the listing update or view event occurred. v2_train_00742 - Over the past 14 days, for each logical API, which 3 hours of the day had the worst average backend wait time?
business enterprise_backtick rolling moderate 782 tok 3 tables rolling_window time_extract_format
Over the past 14 days, for each logical API, which 3 hours of the day had the worst average backend wait time?
WITH "hourly_stats" AS (
  SELECT 
    "apiName",
    EXTRACT(HOUR FROM "__time") AS "hour_of_day",
    AVG("upstreamLatencyMs") AS "avg_backend_wait"
  FROM "apiGatewayRaw"
  WHERE "__time" >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '14' DAY
  GROUP BY 1, 2
),
"ranked_hours" AS (
  SELECT 
    "apiName",
    "hour_of_day",
    "avg_backend_wait",
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "apiName" ORDER BY "avg_backend_wait" DESC) AS "rn"
  FROM "hourly_stats"
)
SELECT 
  "apiName",
  "hour_of_day",
  "avg_backend_wait"
FROM "ranked_hours"
WHERE "rn" <= 3

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Edge cache access records from a content delivery network. This is the event-level table for CDN edge delivery: high volume, one row per edge request. A question asking for a running total or a current snapshot may be better served by a dimension table instead. NULL-safe aggregation: `confidence_score_v2` IS NOT NULL is mandatory when aggregating `confidence_score_v2`. `origin_host` is a per-record identifier, so DISTINCT counts on it are forbidden; count rows. -- **Glossary** -- - **Group-9 edge request**: rows where `pop_code` is one of `iad2`, `gru2`, `sin1` -- - **Pod-R edge request**: records where `cache_status` is `BYPASS` or `REVALIDATED` -- - **content-type-series edge request**: rows where `content_type` starts with `scrip` __time TIMESTAMP Time the edge node served the object pop_code VARCHAR Point-of-presence that served the request (one of: lhr1, iad2, fra3, nrt1, gru2, sin1, syd1) cache_status VARCHAR Edge cache outcome content_type VARCHAR MIME family of the object (one of: image, video, script, html, font, json) protocol VARCHAR Wire protocol (possible values: h2, h3, http1.1) client_country VARCHAR ISO-3166 alpha-2 country of the client (one of: GB, US, DE, JP, BR, SG, AU, IN) object_key VARCHAR Cache key of the requested object origin_host VARCHAR Origin the edge would fall back to bytes_served BIGINT Bytes written to the client ttfb_ms BIGINT Time to first byte, in milliseconds origin_fetch_ms BIGINT Time ASSIGNED TERM (multi_term): Pod-R edge request -- the SQL must apply exactly this definition

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Order lifecycle records from a food delivery platform. Use this table for questions scoped to food delivery; it is the system of record for individual orders, not a daily rollup. ### INSTRUCTIONS * Each updated_by_id maps to exactly one record, so counting orders by it is a simple COUNT. * Unique updated by names must be computed exactly (COUNT(DISTINCT `updated_by_name`)); HLL-style approximations are off limits. Business terms: - Kind-6 order - any row in which `restaurant_id` is in ('r-018', 'r-032') - restaurant-id-family order - rows where `restaurant_id` starts with `r-01` - recently active customer - a `customer_id` that has at least one row in the last 30 days - other-promo-code order - rows where `promo_code` is not one of `FIRST10`, `none` Columns: __time TIMESTAMP, restaurant_id VARCHAR, order_channel VARCHAR, fulfilment VARCHAR, promo_code VARCHAR, customer_id VARCHAR, courier_id VARCHAR, delivery_fee DOUBLE, prep_minutes BIGINT, items_count BIGINT, dietary_flags VARCHAR, settled_on VARCHAR, updated_by_id VARCHAR, updated_by_name VARCHAR, last_modified_source VARCHAR, workflow_state VARCHAR, workflow_substate VARCHAR, approval_status VARCHAR, owner_id VARCHAR, previous_owner_id VARCHAR, owning_team VARCHAR, escalation_level BIGINT, sla_breached_flag BIGINT, retry_count BIGINT, created_by_id VARCHAR, created_by_name VARCHAR, created_by_email VARCHAR, data_quality_flag VARCHAR, department_code VARCHAR, risk_tier VARCHAR, timezone_name VARCHAR, integr ASSIGNED TERM (not_in): other-promo-code order -- the SQL must apply exactly this definition

High cardinality. | | upstream_host | VARCHAR | YES | Backend instance that served the call. | | status_code | BIGINT | YES | | | gateway_late

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Player session summaries from a live-service title. Use this table for questions scoped to gaming; it is the system of record for individual sessions, not a daily rollup. # 1. Counting sessions? `player_id` is unique, therefore skip DISTINCT. # If someone says "Class-M session", they mean rows where `platform` is one of `mobile`, `playstation`, `xbox`. # If someone says "Set-E session", they mean rows where `region` is `sa` or `game_mode` is `ranked`. # If someone says "recently active player", they mean a `player_id` with any activity in the last 90 days. __time TIMESTAMP player_id STRING platform STRING game_mode STRING region STRING duration_seconds LONG xp_earned LONG datasource: ds_water_utility # Telemetry and meter reads from municipal water network endpoints. Use this table for questions scoped to water utility network metering; it is the system of record for individual meter reads, not a daily rollup. # 1. records created by tests: always excluded, via `is_test_record` = 0. # 2. How many unique created by ids? Answer with COUNT(DISTINCT `created_by_id`); estimates are not acceptable. # Reference-set meter read means rows where `customer_class` is one of `residential`, `commercial`, `municipal`. # Low-flow-rate meter read means records where `flow_rate_gpm` <= 1.9. __time TIMESTAMP customer_class STRING meter_model

v2_train_03489 - Last month, for predictions with the 'guardrail' flag, what was the daily count of requests and the cumulative
business yaml last_period moderate 3283 tok 3 tables calendar_window mvd time_extract_format
Last month, for predictions with the 'guardrail' flag, what was the daily count of requests and the cumulative count of requests up to that day?
WITH "daily_stats" AS (
  SELECT
    TIME_FORMAT(__time, 'yyyy-MM-dd') AS "day",
    COUNT(*) AS "daily_count"
  FROM "ml_inference_daily"
  WHERE __time >= TIME_SHIFT(TIME_FLOOR(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'P1M'), 'P1M', -1)
    AND __time < TIME_FLOOR(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'P1M')
    AND MV_CONTAINS(feature_flags, 'guardrail')
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  "day",
  "daily_count",
  SUM("daily_count") OVER (ORDER BY "day" ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS "cumulative_count"
FROM "daily_stats"
ORDER BY 1

daily bytes for core-01 past 30 days with cumulative sum
WITH "daily_traffic" AS (
  SELECT
    TIME_FLOOR(__time, 'P1D') AS "day",
    SUM(bytes) AS "daily_bytes"
  FROM network_flows_daily
  WHERE exporter = 'core-01'
    AND __time >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '30' DAY
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  "day",
  "daily_bytes",
  SUM("daily_bytes") OVER (ORDER BY "day") AS "cumulative_bytes"
FROM "daily_traffic"
ORDER BY 1

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Tracking moderation actions taken on user-generated content. This is the event-level table for social-platform content moderation: high volume, one row per moderation action. A question asking for a running total or a current snapshot may be better served by a dimension table instead. The distinct count of `reviewer_id` has to be precise, so approximations are not acceptable. Counting moderation actions? `updated_by_name` is unique, therefore skip DISTINCT. written-content moderation action: any row in which `content_type` is in ('text_post', 'comment') age-days-to-review-latency ratio: SUM(`user_account_age_days`) / SUM(`review_latency_hours`) Family-C moderation action: records where either `language` = 'en' or `sla_breached_flag` = 0 high-age-days moderation action: records where `user_account_age_days` >= 1450 ### Columns: `__time` (TIMESTAMP, NOT NULL): Time the moderation decision was recorded. Becomes `__time`, the only TIMESTAMP column. `content_type` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): Format of the flagged content. `action_taken` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): The final moderation decision (one of: kept, removed, shadowbanned, warning_issued, escalated). `reviewer_type` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): Type of entity that made the decision (values: automod, human_reviewer, user_appeal_board). `language` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): Detected language of the content (one of: en, es, fr, ar, hi, zh, other). `content_id` (VARCHAR, NULLABLE): Unique identifier for the piece of content. `reviewer_id` (VARCHAR, NULLA

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Individual transactions processed by a fleet of automated teller machines. Use this table for questions scoped to bank ATM network transactions; it is the system of record for individual ATM transactions, not a daily rollup. Do not apply DISTINCT to `customer_account_id` when counting -- there is one record for each value. The distinct count of `updated_by_id` has to be precise, so approximations are not acceptable. -- Business terms: -- - Group-8 ATM transaction - records where `card_network` is `on_us`, `visa` or `mastercard` -- - dispensed-to-processing-latency ratio - the ratio of summed `amount_dispensed` to summed `processing_latency` -- - other-auth-result ATM transaction - records where `auth_result` is anything other than `approved` or `declined_bad_pin` -- - lately active terminal - a `terminal_id` that has at least one row in the last 30 days __time TIMESTAMP Time when the ATM transaction was initiated atm_model VARCHAR Hardware model of the terminal card_network VARCHAR The network processing the card (one of: visa, mastercard, amex, discover, on_us) auth_result VARCHAR Whether the transaction was approved or declined currency_code VARCHAR Local currency of the ATM terminal_id VARCHAR Unique identifier for the ATM hardware customer_account_id VARCHAR Hashed identifier for the customer account amount_dispensed DOUBLE The actual monetary amount dispensed surcharge_fee DOUBLE Fee levied by the ATM operator processing_la

Rules / glossary as printed in the prompt: Scan events from a parcel and freight network. This is the event-level table for freight logistics: high volume, one row per parcel scan. A question asking for a running total or a current snapshot may be better served by a dimension table instead. Note: Filter every query to `is_test_record` = 0 so records created by tests stay out; count rows, not distinct created_by_name values, to get the number of parcel scans. By Italy-or-Ireland parcel scan we mean any row in which `dest_country` is in ('IT', 'IE'). By active correlation we mean a `correlation_id` that has at least one row in the last 60 days. By other-carrier-code parcel scan we mean records where `carrier_code` is anything other than `TNT`. - __time (TIMESTAMP) - Time the parcel was scanned - carrier_code (VARCHAR) - Carrier handling the leg (values: DHL, UPS, FEDX, DPD, GLS, TNT) - scan_type (VARCHAR) - What the scan recorded (one of: pickup, in_transit, customs, out_for_delivery, delivered, exception) - service_level (VARCHAR) - Service purchased (one of: economy, standard, express, same_day) - origin_country (VARCHAR) - Country the shipment left (values: DE, NL, PL, CZ, FR, ES) - dest_country (VARCHAR) - Country the shipment is bound for (possible values: GB, IT, SE, PT, AT, IE) - tracking_number (VARCHAR) - Parcel tracking number - hub_code (VARCHAR) - Sorting hub that produced the scan - weight_kg (DOUBLE) - Billable weight in kilograms - declared_value_eur (DOUBLE) - Declared customs v

updated_by_idstringIdentifier of the last user or service to modify the record.
updated_by_namestringDisplay name of the last modifier.
last_modified_sourcestringSystem that last wrote the record.
workflow_statestringCurrent step in the processing workflow.
workflow_substatestringFiner-grained state within workflow_state.
approval_statusstringApproval outcome, where applicable.
owner_idstringCurrent owner of the record.
previous_owner_idstringOwner before the last reassignment, or blank.
owning_teamstringTeam the current owner belongs to.
channel_detailstringFiner-grained channel than the primary entity column.
record_versionstringSchema version the record was written under.
